answer: Like a lotus rooted in a shared lagoon, each agent's standing grows from its web of interactions. In a trust-graph defence, new identities must earn links from many unrelated, established agents, and random walks from verified nodes measure how deeply an identity is embedded in the honest region. A Sybil cluster may spin up hundreds of fake nodes, but they connect mostly to each other, like boats tied to the same jetty — the walks rarely cross into them. Building the dense, diverse ties a real identity needs costs an attacker months of real work per fake, so mass forgery becomes uneconomic.
